name: Disorder of Methionine Cycle and Sulfur Amino Acid Metabolism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biochemical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Methionine Cycle Disorders

criteria.description: Persistent elevated plasma homocysteine levels above age-specific reference ranges
Demonstrated deficiency or dysfunction of enzymes involved in methionine cycle (e.g., CBS, MTHFR)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding methionine cycle or sulfur amino acid metabolism enzymes
Presence of characteristic clinical manifestations such as thromboembolism or developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated homocysteine plus either enzyme deficiency or pathogenic genetic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires biochemical confirmation and genetic testing for definitive classification.

pathognomonic.notes: Markedly elevated homocysteine in plasma is characteristic
Displacement of the ocular lens due to connective tissue abnormalities
searchTerms: lens out of place in eye

pathognomonic.notes: Venous or arterial thrombosis often occurs early

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Tall stature, long limbs, and arachnodactyly
Reduced bone mineral density leading to fractures
Generalized or focal seizures may be present

occasional.notes: Ischemic events due to vascular involvement
Enlarged liver due to metabolic stress
Reduced muscle tone in infants and children
Including nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain

rare.notes: Hearing impairment due to nerve damage

laboratory: Elevated plasma homocysteine and methionine levels
Low cysteine and altered sulfur amino acid profiles
Reduced activity of cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) or other methionine cycle enzymes
imaging: MRI brain showing ischemic lesions or white matter abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CBS, MTHFR, or related genes involved in methionine metabolism

distinguishingFeatures: Markedly elevated homocysteine with early-onset lens dislocation
Metabolic acidosis with elevated methylmalonic acid

redFlags: Early-onset thromboembolism without typical risk factors
Severe hyperhomocysteinemia detected on routine screening
references: Mudd SH, et al. Disorders of transsulfuration. In: Scriver CR, et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
